tools.detail: Small model the Decisions API is built on; keeps image understanding, broad language support and safety

claims: Decisions API gives the model a predefined set of options to choose from -- routing a request, classifying an image, deciding which agent to call next
By focusing the model on that choice it is 'extremely fast' while keeping image understanding, broad language support and safety precautions
Demo: 'Find a one-way, nonstop flight from SFO to Seattle on Friday after 6 a.m.' routed into a Flights UI
on_screen_only: Stage slide: 'Decisions API -- In preview' with demo prompt 'Find a one-way, nonstop flight from SFO to Seattle on Friday after 6 a.m.' and a Flights results screen with date picker
Caption tags @OpenAI; creator filming from the Dev Day audience

relevance.why: A fast, cheap 'pick one of N options' API is useful inside our apps for routing/classification steps (intent routing, triage, next-agent selection), and it is the OpenAI answer to Jev. We are Claude-first, but the pattern -- constrained-choice calls with a small model -- is worth copying with Haiku + structured outputs.

implement_score.why: Nothing to do yet: preview, no pricing. Keep in mind for routing layers; we can already do constrained choice with Claude structured outputs. Revisit when GA with pricing.

verify: Decisions API availability, pricing, latency (the news article in a sibling video says 150 ms) and whether it returns confidence scores
What 'Luna' is in OpenAI's lineup (smallest/cheapest model?) and its context/image limits
Whether the equivalent is achievable with Claude Haiku + tool-use enum outputs at similar cost
